full_text:
Hey, everyone! It’s year three of my trench breakdowns for *Fantasy Points*, which means that the NFL preseason is just around the corner. I know the offensive line isn’t the sexiest position group to talk about, but how the big boys up front perform directly affects the rest of the offense. If you’re on the pulse of OL play, you have an advantage for fantasy.

Once again, the *__“games are won and lost in the trenches”__* quote came true in the biggest game of the year, as the Seahawks’ pass rush put __Drake Maye__ in a torture chamber in Super Bowl LX. It’s overused and cliché at this point, but as a player, coach, scout, or fan, that quote should always have a spot in the back of your mind.

Before I get to my rankings, I want to quickly recap how I evaluate offensive lines. This process came from my 10 years working in the Cleveland Browns’ personnel department. Keep these factors in mind when making roster decisions.

### What makes a good offensive line?

+   __Continuity, Continuity, Continuity__ — The more a unit plays together, the better the communication and overall quality of play. I value four of five starters returning higher than spending the most money in free agency.

+   __Depth__ — OL injuries can derail any unit (think Tampa Bay), but having quality replacements can keep a team competitive. You can never have too many linemen, but they have to be capable.

+   __Quality additions__ — Turnover typically happens every year with OL groups. Adding the right veteran or draft pick could be the missing piece to becoming elite.

+   __Veteran/Youth split__ — Playing offensive line as a rookie or second-year player is incredibly difficult, so having quality vets can speed up a young player’s development.

+   __Coaching__ — OL is the most technique-heavy position. Having the right person in charge of the room is crucial. I had first-hand experience with this in Cleveland. We hired __Bill Callahan__ in 2020 after years of questionable coaching, and a good unit became one of the league’s best.

+   __Scheme fit__ — Can these players fit the schemes we’re trying to run? Coaches and GMs have to ask this question; otherwise, the OL will struggle.

A quality offensive line has to be good in both phases. Pass protection has become incredibly important, but being able to grind out a game on the ground is critical to winning a championship. Good offensive lines often go unnoticed because they’re doing everything right.

Let’s get into the rankings.

### Scott DiBenedetto’s 2026 NFL Offensive Line Rankings

\>

\> $ Denotes New Acquisition

\>

\> / denotes a potential battle or a top backup

#### 1\. __Denver Broncos__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 2

#### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Garett Bolles__

LG __Ben Powers / Kage Casey \*__

C __Luke Wattenberg__

RG __Quinn Meinerz__

RT __Mike McGlinchey__

The first of my 2025 “Elite” offensive lines is the Broncos. This unit was steadily at the top of the list all season long, and returns all five starters for the third straight year. It’s tough to believe this group won’t be elite again, but there is a “major” change: __Davis Webb__ taking over as OC. Yes, __Sean Payton__ is still the play-caller, but changes in messaging and presentation could be more impactful than expected.

I feel like I could copy and paste what I wrote last year, as all five guys are returning. __Garett Bolles__ and __Quinn Meinerz__ were quietly the best LT and RG duo in the game last year. C __Luke Wattenberg__ was excellent, and RT __Mike McGlinchey__ was well above average in the run game.

The weak link was LG __Ben Powers__. He clearly struggled in both phases, and it’s no shock that Denver selected __Kage Casey__ in the draft. I’m not sure if Casey, as a fourth-round pick, will usurp Powers, but Payton is already looking ahead.

The Broncos were rolling last year before a freak injury to __Bo Nix__ against Buffalo. That moment likely kept Denver out of Super Bowl 60, but the team is built for another run.

#### 2\. __Indianapolis Colts__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 7

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Bernhard Raimann / Blake Freeland__

LG __Quenton Nelson__

C __Tanor Bortolini__

RG __Matt Goncalves / Jalen Farmer \*__

RT __Jalen Travis__

Don’t sleep on Indianapolis’s offensive line heading into 2026. The Colts were rolling into their Week 11 bye at 8-2, then the wheels came off, and they lost seven straight to end 2025. Their offensive line was the engine that got them those eight wins, as __Jonathan Taylor__ racked up nearly 1,600 yards behind this group. I’m expecting more of the same with four starters returning.

__Bernhard Raimann__ and __Quenton Nelson__ form one of the toughest left sides in the league. Nelson has been elite since year one, and Raimann quickly became a steady force, earning a four-year extension last summer. C __Tanor Bortolini__ was an elite run blocker last year, but will need to step up in protection, and RT __Jalen Travis__ did well filling in for __Braden Smith__ for four games.

The question marks are: will Travis hold up over 17 games, and will RG __Matt Goncalves__ continue to be the weak link? Goncalves wasn’t terrible last season, but was noticeably not as productive as his linemates.

I’m excited about this unit again, as it has been consistently above average to elite for years. There was little turnover this offseason, so the Colts should be solid up front in 2026.

#### 3\. __Chicago Bears__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 15

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Braxton Jones / Ozzy Trapilo__

LG __Joe Thuney__

C __Garrett Bradbury $__

RG __Jonah Jackson__

RT __Darnell Wright / Theo Benedet__

__Ryan Poles__ and __Ben Johnson__’s offensive line investments worked nearly to perfection in 2025, as the Bears snuck into the “Elite” tier at the end of the season, despite the revolving door at LT. All but one of the starting group returns for 2026, and Chicago is poised to make another run.

__Darnell Wright__ anchored the right side as one of the best run blockers in the league, and RG __Jonah Jackson__ followed suit with a quality season in the run game. LG __Joe Thuney__ was unshockingly outstanding in protection and grinded out a strong run-blocking campaign. What excites me most about this group is that __Braxton__ __Jones__’ absence didn’t derail it.

Jones made it through Week 4 before sitting for two weeks and being placed on IR. __Theo Benedet__ and __Ozzy Trapilo__ held firm before Trapilo’s late-season patellar tendon injury. Jones has to rebound in 2026, but the Bears have quality depth behind him.

The biggest change is at center, as __Garrett Bradbury__ was acquired via trade after __Drew Dalman__ retired. Bradbury was below average last year in New England, but should fit into Chicago’s well-established OL. This group should be in the top 10 all season.

#### 4\. __Tampa Bay Buccaneers__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 3

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Tristan Wirfs__

LG __Ben Bredeson__

C __Graham Barton__

RG __Cody Mauch__

RT __Luke Goedeke / Justin Skule $__

Tampa Bay is another team that brings back all five starters, but I’m not as certain about them as I am about Denver. The Bucs were firmly in my “Elite” tier all of 2024, yet ended 2025 below-average. The injury bug hit Tampa Bay hard up front, so I can give them a bit of a pass, but this unit needs to rebound majorly in 2026.

__Tristan Wirfs__ and __Luke Goedeke__ form one of the best tackle combos in the league. Wirfs was elite despite missing the first three games and Week 17. Goedeke also battled foot issues that put him on IR to start the season. These two must stay healthy. __Justin Skule__ is also a quality depth/insurance signing on the edge.

The interior was much more of a mess, caused by both injuries and poor play. __Ben Bredeson__ was lost to a late-season knee injury, but was majorly struggling in the run game. __Graham Barton__ was flat-out bad in protection all season, and __Cody Mauch__ tore his meniscus in Week 2. The Bucs ultimately have to flush 2025 as a lost year up front, but I have faith that this group will return to form if it can avoid the injury bug.

#### 5\. __Philadelphia Eagles__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 1

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Jordan Mailata__

LG __Landon Dickerson__

C __Cam Jurgens__

RG __Tyler Steen / Micah Morris \*__

RT __Lane Johnson__

I can’t say that 2025 was a banner year for my projected best offensive line. Philadelphia may have gone through a Super Bowl hangover that lasted all season, and ultimately ended with __A.J. Brown__’s departure. This unit was ultimately a big disappointment, but all five starters return.

__Jordan Mailata__ and __Lane Johnson__ are still arguably the best tackle pair in the game. Johnson is closer to the end of his career, but these two remain a major force. __Cam Jurgens__ and __Tyler Steen__ were fine in their first years starting at C and RG, respectively. Steen was better overall, and Jurgens will have to improve in protection.

The unit’s biggest issue last year was __Landon Dickerson__. He suffered a meniscus injury in training camp that lingered all season, so he was clearly not the same player, particularly in protection. __Jalen Hurts__ makes life difficult on his line, but Dickerson’s injury didn’t help matters.

If Dickerson returns to full strength, the Eagles should rebound up front. That said, there are a bunch of changes, as longtime OL coach __Jeff Stoutland__ has moved on. __Chris Kuper__ takes over the room, and __Sean Mannion__ comes in as OC. This group is too vet-heavy to let those changes affect it, but don’t be surprised if the Eagles get off to a slow start.

#### 6\. __Los Angeles Rams__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 9

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Alaric Jackson__

LG __Steve Avila / Beaux Limmer__

C __Coleman Shelton__

RG __Kevin Dotson__

RT __Warren McClendon Jr. / Keagen Trost \*__

Assuming this unit has all five projected starters, the Rams are once again poised to be one of the better offensive lines in the league. I left this unit for dead once the injury bug hit early in 2025, but Los Angeles was pushing for “Elite” status by the end of the season.

Veteran RG __Kevin Dotson__ anchors this group and was highly productive last year, despite playing for a stretch with a heavily wrapped hand. RT __Warren McClendon__ was much better than I expected in 2025, which makes me confident the right side will be dangerous. __Steve Avila__ and __Coleman Shelton__ have some things to clean up inside. Shelton, in particular, was replacement level in protection, so watch for __Beaux Limmer__ to see some time if needed.

There’s a big question mark around LT __Alaric Jackson__. On the field, he was solidly above-average in both phases last year, but he’s facing a [domestic violence charge](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7345000/2026/06/09/rams-alaric-jackson-arrested-domestic-violence/) heading into 2026. Jackson was the team’s most consistent blocker last year, so losing him for any stretch would be rough.

The Rams could make a Super Bowl run in 2026, but not if they endure another season with many OL lineup changes due to injuries.

#### 7\. __Buffalo Bills__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 6

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Dion Dawkins__

LG __Alec Anderson / Austin Corbett $__

C __Connor McGovern__

RG __O’Cyrus Torrence__

RT __Spencer Brown__

The Bills once again have major continuity up front heading into 2026, as four of the five starters return. __Joe Brady__ takes over as head coach, but that shouldn’t be an issue, as he was the offensive coordinator for the last two and a half years. Buffalo’s window is still open, and this is the least amount of change that can happen when a new head coach is hired. But priority No. 1 is keeping __Josh Allen__ upright.

__Dion Dawkins__ and __Spencer Brown__ return to anchor the edges. They aren’t on the same level as the pairs in Philadelphia and Tampa Bay, but these two are quietly a top-five duo. __O’Cyrus Torrence__ returns for year four at RG, and __Connor McGovern__ is back after Allen convinced the front office to give his center $52 million.

The only new starter is __Alec Anderson__ at LG, but he’s far from a guy who just walked in off the street. Anderson has been Buffalo’s jumbo TE the last few years, and saw some extended run at LG in 2025. The biggest change up front is the new OL coach, __Pat Meyer__, replacing __Aaron Kromer__. This group is so vet-heavy that a new voice shouldn’t drastically alter things, but this unit had a clear problem protecting Allen, and it needs to be fixed quickly.

#### 8\. __Detroit Lions__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 5

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Penei Sewell__

LG __Christian Mahogany / Ben Bartch $__

C __Cade Mays $ / Juice Scruggs $__

RG __Tate Ratledge__

RT __Blake Miller \* / Larry Borom $__

Detroit, like Baltimore, has seen a major shake-up with its offensive line. Just two years ago, the Lions had a top-two OL in football. There was a slight regression last year with essentially the same crew, and now there are major changes with four positions seeing new starters.

LG __Christian Mahogany__ is the only returning starter playing the same position, and 2025 was fairly disastrous, particularly in protection. __Tate Ratledge__ moves to RG in year two. He was adequate as a rookie, but he also needs work in pass pro. The big move is __Penei Sewell__ (finally) moving to LT after __Taylor Decker__’s release. Sewell is arguably the best tackle in football, regardless of side, so he should be fine on the left.

After those three, five new faces could all see time on the field. Rookie RT __Blake Miller__ replaces Sewell and should be a capable starter. His athletic limitations will keep his ceiling low, but his floor is fairly high, thanks to starting over 50 games at Clemson. Veteran __Larry Borom__ comes in as Miller’s backup. The Lions also added __Cade Mays__, __Juice Scruggs__, and __Ben Bartch__ in the interior. Mays is slated to start at center, but don’t be surprised if all three see time this year.

Also, like Baltimore, Detroit is in a new offensive era with __Drew Petzing__ taking over as OC. We’ll have to let Petzing’s system play out, but I’d put a lot of faith in the Lions’ veteran-heavy offense to make plays when it matters. That said, things start up front, and this is the most change that __Jared Goff__ will have had to deal with from his OL since he’s been in Detroit.

#### 9\. __Los Angeles Chargers__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 10

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Rashawn Slater__

LG __Jake Slaughter \*__

C __Tyler Biadasz $__

RG __Cole Strange $ / Kayode Awosika $__

RT __Joe Alt__

Both Los Angeles teams were snake-bitten with offensive line issues last season, but the Chargers definitely “won” that race after losing __Rashawn Slater__ and __Joe Alt__ at different points. With those two healthy and three other changes, __Justin Herbert__ essentially has a brand new offensive line blocking for him.

Slater returns after brutally tearing his patellar tendon during training camp. That should have been a sign of things to come for Los Angeles, as Alt played only six games after suffering multiple ankle injuries. These are the two cornerstones of this unit, so it’s still impressive that the Chargers got to the playoffs without either of them.

The real changes are across the interior as __Tyler Biadasz__ and __Cole Strange__ come over in free agency, and __Jake Slaughter__ comes in as a second-round pick. Biadasz was solid last year, but Strange is a replacement-level player. Slaughter should eventually become the starting center, but he’s more than capable of being a productive guard in year one.

Expect a slow start from this group as all five get used to playing with each other, but the tackles and Biadasz should carry the unit early.

#### 10\. __Atlanta Falcons__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 12

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Jake Matthews / Wanya Morris $__

LG __Matthew Bergeron__

C __Ryan Neuzil__

RG __Chris Lindstrom__

RT __Jawaan Taylor $__

The Falcons just couldn’t get out of their own way last season. Atlanta had a plethora of talent on both sides of the ball (much of which is returning), but a midseason five-game losing streak sank the year. __Kevin Stefanski__ now takes over as head coach, and his offensive line is built for his wide zone rushing attack.

The ironman __Jake Matthews__ returns at LT. He’s still superb in protection, but his run blocking took a major dip last year. __Matthew Bergeron__ is still getting better heading into year four to complete a quality left side. C __Ryan Neuzil__ and RG __Chris Lindstrom__ round out the returning starters as a pair of elite run blockers who could be better in protection. I’m still high on the returning group for Atlanta, as their play styles mesh extremely well with Stefanski’s system.

However, __Jawann Taylor__ could derail the entire unit. Taylor comes over from Kansas City as a cap casualty after failing as the Chiefs’ big free agent signing a few years ago. He never lived up to the billing in KC and was a replacement-level run blocker last year.

Taylor scares me, but I’ll lean on the rest of the group and quality coaching, as __Bill Callahan__ reconnects with Stefanski. This OL should be in or near the top 10 all season.

#### 11\. __Carolina Panthers__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 18

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Rasheed Walker / Ikem Ekwonu__

LG __Damien Lewis__

C __Luke Fortner $__

RG __Robert Hunt__

RT __Taylor Moton / Monroe Freeling \*__

Carolina’s offensive line has been trending up the last couple of seasons and should push to be a top-half or top 10 unit this year. The Panthers overperformed in 2025 and 2026 will come down to quarterback play, but __Bryce Young__ will have a quality group blocking for him.

Four starters return for Carolina, anchored by __Ikem Ekwonu__ (currently injured with a torn patellar, so it’ll be a while before he returns) and __Taylor Moton__ at the tackle spots. Moton remains reliable heading into year 10. RG __Robert Hunt__ returns after missing most of 2025 with a torn biceps, and LG __Damien Lewis__ will look to build off an exceptional year in both phases.

The new faces are: __Luke Fortner__, who comes over from New Orleans to replace __Austin Corbett__ at C, __Rasheed Walker,__ over from Green Bay and likely starting for Ekwonu, and first-round pick __Monroe Freeling__. Fortner is on a super cheap deal after an impressive 2025. Walker was better in protection last season, and offers experience on the blindside. Freeling should become Moton’s long-term replacement, although he has the build and athleticism to play on either side. He might have to play right away opposite Moton given Ekwonu’s January patellar tendon tear.

With the exception of Ekwonu’s injury problems, things remain bright in Carolina.

#### 12\. __Dallas Cowboys__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 20

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Tyler Guyton__

LG __Tyler Smith__

C __Cooper Beebe / Nick Leverett__

RG __Tyler Booker__

RT __Terence Steele / Drew Shelton \*__

The Cowboys' offensive line overperformed my expectations last year. I didn’t think the group would be awful, but I didn't anticipate it would become a top-10 unit by the end of the season. All five starters are back, so expect a solid season from the boys up front.

LG __Tyler Smith__ is the rock that holds things together in Dallas, and he put in an elite run-blocking season last year. C __Cooper Beebe__ was average or better in both phases, and RG __Tyler Booker__ was an outstanding run blocker as a rookie.

If there are questions, they’re at tackle, as __Terence Steele__ and __Tyler Guyton__ aren’t the best pair. Steele is a strong enough run blocker to survive, but, in my opinion, this is a make-or-break year for Guyton. The continuity should naturally get this group close to the top 10, but I’m still on the fence about the tackle situation.

#### 13\. __Jacksonville Jaguars__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 21

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Cole Van Lanen / Walker Little__

LG __Ezra Cleveland / Emmanuel Pregnon \*__

C __Robert Hainsey__

RG __Patrick Mekari__

RT __Anton Harrison__

Jacksonville should have big expectations for 2026. They fell short against Buffalo in the playoffs, but this team had a lot working for it last year. The offensive line, in particular, should be solid with four-plus starters returning (I’ll clarify). The Jaguars will ultimately go as far as __Trevor Lawrence__ takes them, but he should be comfortable in the pocket.

I’ll say that none of the returning starters were particularly impressive last year in year one of __Liam Coen__. LG __Ezra Cleveland__ was firmly the best and was the group’s best in protection. C __Robert Hainsey__ struggled in both phases, and RT __Anton Harrison__ was slightly better. My biggest disappointment was with RG __Patrick Mekari__. He’s my favorite utility lineman, but a full season at one spot apparently wasn’t the best thing.

The big change is that __Cole Van Lanen__ will now start at LT. Van Lanen was excellent in the Mekari-esque utility role, playing both guard and tackle spots in 2025. Will he continue to be solid or crumble playing only one spot?

Be on the lookout for rookie guard __Emmanuel Pregnon__. The Oregon product is built to be a downhill grinder, so be aware of any run scheme changes if he sees extended time in 2026.

#### 14\. __Seattle Seahawks__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 30

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Charles Cross__

LG __Grey Zabel__

C __Jalen Sundell / Olu Oluwatimi__

RG __Anthony Bradford / Beau Stephens \*__

RT __Abraham Lucas__

Hand up! I missed on Seattle’s offensive line last year, slotting them in at No. 30 heading into 2025. Were they world beaters? No. Seattle was one of the league’s worst rushing teams in the regular season, and __Sam Darnold__’s quick time to throw (2.52 seconds) saved this unit more often than not. But this group deserved much more credit than I gave it, and the best part is that all five starters return for 2026.

__Charles Cross__ and __Abe Lucas__ anchor the edges. They were solidly above-average in both phases and should carry positive momentum into 2026. Their protection grades will be somewhat inflated, thanks to Darnold and the scheme, but these two are very capable tackles. __Grey Zabel__ will look to build on a fine rookie season, and __Jalen Sundell__ proved that he’s a steady blocker in the middle.

The issue up front for Seattle is RG __Anthony Bradford__. He shockingly started every game last year despite being one of the worst RGs in the NFL. He particularly struggled in protection. Bradford is entering the final year of his contract, so could we see __Olu Oluwatimi__ or rookie __Beau Stephens__ at RG at any point?

Seattle is coming off a Super Bowl victory, but there are changes on offense as __Brian Fluery__ takes over as OC following __Klint Kubiak__'s departure. The Seahawks are built for another run, but how long will it take to get rolling on offense?

#### 15\. __Baltimore Ravens__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 4

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Ronnie Stanley__

LG __Olaivavega Ioane \*__

C __Danny Pinter $ / Jovaughn Gwyn $__

RG __John Simpson $__

RT __Roger Rosengarten__

I’ve been a Ravens OL supporter for the last couple of seasons, mainly because of continuity and quality coaching. Unfortunately, both are gone in 2026, as only two starters return and __Jesse Minter__ takes over as head coach.

The returners are both tackles, as vet stalwart __Ronnie Stanley__ anchors the edge with young RT __Roger Rosengarten__. Stanley was still effective in year 10, but I was very impressed with how well Rosengarten did in year two. This is a strong duo that will have to lead the unit. Meanwhile, the interior has been completely reworked after losing __Tyler Linderbaum__ and both guards.

The exciting piece is rookie LG __Vega Ioane__. Without a doubt, he was the best guard in the draft, and he has the build and mentality to be a road-grating Ravens run blocker. However, I’m less fired up about the other two additions. RG __John Simpson__ returns for his second stint with Baltimore after signing a three-year deal, and C __Danny Pinter__ comes over from Indianapolis on a one-year contract. Neither was particularly strong last season, so expect a slow start from the interior three.

It’s a new era in Baltimore for __Lamar Jackson__ and the rest of the offense. Jackson will make plays, but I have a hard time believing in his offensive line.

#### 16\. __Arizona Cardinals__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 8

##### Projected Starting Lineups

LT __Paris Johnson__

LG __Isaac Seumalo $__

C __Hjalte Froholdt__

RG __Chase Bisontis \*__

RT __Elijah WIlkinson $ / Oli Udoh $__

Man, was I a fan of the Cardinals heading into 2025. The offensive line got me fired up with how it ended 2024, and then the unit had little turnover at the start of last season. This group ultimately finished firmly in my “Average” tier, and now three new faces have stepped in after.

LT __Paris Johnson__ and C __Hjalte Froholdt__ return after steady 2025 campaigns. I have more faith in Johnson to carry over his performance, as Froholdt is dealing with two new guards on either side of him. Vets __Isaac Seumalo__ and __Elijah Wilkinson__ come over from Pittsburgh and Atlanta, respectively. Seumalo was excellent in protection last year, while Wilkinson will need to be better in both phases.

The big addition is RG __Chase Bisontis__. The 34th overall pick was one of my favorite interior linemen in the draft, and I would have been very comfortable spending a first-round pick on him. He’s strong, quick, and athletic enough for both rushing schemes and should be starting for the next decade.

I’m not expecting much from Arizona’s offense this year with the quarterback issues, but the offensive line should be a top-half unit.

#### 17\. __Minnesota Vikings__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 14

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Christian Darrisaw / Caleb Tiernan \*__

LG __Donovan Jackson__

C __Blake Brandel__

RG __Will Fries__

RT __Brian O’Neill / Ryan Van Demark $__

Minnesota is another group I expected more from last season, but the OL could never put it all together. There’s one big change and a couple other new faces up front. Oh, and there’s (most likely) a new quarterback in __Kyler Murray__.

The good news is that __Christian Darrisaw__, __Donovan Jackson__, __Will Fries__, and __Brian O’Neill__ are all back. Yes, I typically favor continuity, but it’s nuanced with Minnesota. O’Neill was the best of the group in both phases, but Darrisaw never fully recovered from his major knee injury in 2024 and played only 10 games. Jackson was better than expected in protection as a rookie, but Fries was consistently below-average in 2024. __Blake Brandel__ takes over at C for __Ryan Kelly__, after splitting time between C and LG last year.

There’s a ton of continuity with the group, but the front office signed __Ryan Van Demark__ from Buffalo and drafted __Caleb Tiernan__ in the third round. These feel like insurance moves, and that the powers that be don’t fully trust the unit. The Vikings will compete in the NFC North, but I don’t see Murray getting this group to the postseason.

#### 18\. __San Francisco 49ers__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 16

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Trent Williams__

LG __Connor Colby / Carver Willis \*__

C __Jake Brendel / Brett Toth $__

RG __Dominick Puni__

RT __Colton McKivitz__

2025 was a roller coaster for the 49ers. After enduring a season from hell in 2024, San Francisco was a win away from home-field advantage in the playoffs, but lost at home to Seattle in Week 18, then again on the road in the Divisional Round. The offensive line was the backbone of __Kyle Shanahan__’s offense, but the unit majorly regressed last season.

Future Hall of Famer __Trent Williams__ is back at LT, and was once again elite in *year 16* (!!!). RT __Kolton McKivitz__ carried his weight on the other side, completing one of the best tackle duos in the game. However, the interior left much to be desired last season.

RG __Dominick Puni__ and C __Jake Brendel__ weren’t atrocious, but were far from good in both phases, and then rookie __Connor Colby__ was awful in protection, filling in for __Ben Bartch__. Bartch is gone, so Colby is slated to start at LG, but don’t be shocked if free agent signing __Brett Toth__ or fourth-round pick __Carver Willis__ see time.

San Francisco still has continuity up front and quality coaching to be competitive in the NFC West. I think LG will be a problem and could be a revolving door all season, but I expect the group to rebound in 2026.

#### 19\. __New England Patriots__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 23

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Will Campbell__

LG __Alijah Vera-Tucker $__

C __Jared Wilson__

RG __Mike Onwenu__

RT __Morgan Moses / Caleb Lomu \*__

Have the Patriots been in the headlines for anything this offseason?

After making a surprise run to the Super Bowl, New England turns over two spots on the offensive line that struggled to protect __Drake Maye__ against Seattle. Maye was partially to blame, but this unit had trouble keeping him clean all season, and finished with a modest 4.44 YPC (14th). New England has taken a couple of big swings with the two additions in hopes of making life easier on Maye.

Starting with the returners, LT __Will Campbell__ faded down the stretch and was the focal point of abuse in the playoffs, thanks to a Week 12 knee injury (or because of his short arms?). 2025 was a solid rookie year overall, but he’ll have much to prove that his playoff performance was a fluke. RG __Mike Onwenu__ continued to be a high-level producer, and RT __Morgan Moses__ was solid in year 12, particularly in the run game.

New England made two key additions this offseason. The first is rookie tackle __Caleb Lomu__. The “other” Utah tackle will back up either Campbell or Moses, and could be the long-term option opposite Campbell. He’s another big, athletic tackle, but isn’t ready to see the field. The other move was signing __Alijah Vera-Tucker__ away from the Jets. He didn’t play at all last season after tearing his triceps prior to Week 1. He was a firmly above-average performer in 2024 and is an instant upgrade from __Cole Strange__.

I like the moves New England made, but priority No. 1 has to be keeping Maye upright. Maye himself has to improve his awareness when under pressure, but the Patriots have given him a lot to work with up front.

#### 20\. __New Orleans Saints__ - 2025 Preseason Ranking: 25

LG __David Edwards $__

The Saints’ offensive line is well-suited for a step forward in 2025. That’s not a super-high bar, as they were firmly in my “Yikes” tier at the end of last season. But it’s hard to deny how well the offense played overall down the stretch. __Tyler Shough__ is the man in New Orleans, and year two of __Kellen Moore__’s offense gives me hope.

It’s no surprise that New Orleans couldn’t run the ball in 2025 (31st in YPC, 3.69), but it wasn’t the fault of LT __Kelvin Banks__. There were questions about Banks as a rookie, but he became the team’s most effective run blocker last year, and he was more than serviceable in protection. Unfortunately, that’s where the firm positives stop for the Saints.

All of the other three returning starters were below-average in the run game (well below for RG __Cesar Ruiz__), and I was most disappointed with RT __Taliese Fuaga__. I expected a bigger jump in year two, but I can chalk it up to it being the first year in a new system if he comes out strong in 2026. The big addition is LG __David Edwards__, who comes over from Buffalo. New Orleans gave him a four-year deal, and he’s an instant run game upgrade.

It would be a major disappointment if there isn’t a clear effort to improve the run game in 2026, and Edwards’ arrival creates a solid run blocking left side. I don’t think this unit will finish the season in the top half, but there should be a clear step forward.

#### 21\. __Green Bay Packers__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 13

RT __Zach Tom__

I’ll be honest, I haven’t been able to make much sense of Green Bay’s offensive line the last couple of years. They’re consistently good enough to be around the middle, but the unit hasn’t taken a collective step forward. That said, the Packers are another team where all five projected starters saw time last year, just in a different alignment.

The most consistent performer last season was RT __Zach Tom__. He was solid in both phases and will have to again in 2026. __Jordan Morgan__ will slide over to LT full time (hopefully) after playing everywhere but center last season. __Aaron Banks__ returns at LG after a subpar season, but the real problems for Green Bay are at RG and C.

__Sean Rhyan__ and __Anthony Belton__ played multiple positions last season … but did so at well below replacement level in both phases. __Jager Burton__ comes in as a fifth-round pick, but I wouldn’t be shocked if he saw some time along the interior. I’m interested to see how much losing __Elgton Jenkins__ affects the group.

I want to like this unit more, and the Packers will be in the mix thanks to __Jordan Love__, but the offensive line needs to prove it to me. By the numbers, last year wasn’t pretty, as the group finished in my “Bad” tier. Can they rebound?

#### 22\. __Miami Dolphins__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 28

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Patrick Paul / Jamaree Salyer $__

LG __Kadyn Proctor \*__

C __Aaron Brewer__

RG __Jonah Savaiinaea__

RT __Austin Jackson / Charlie Heck $__

For the mess that was the 2025 Miami Dolphins, the offensive line wasn’t as big an issue as I thought it would be. It wasn’t better than average, but the unit held things together well enough to produce the fourth-best YPC in the league (4.73). However, there’s plenty of work to be done for new head coach __Jeff Hafley__ and offensive coordinator __Bobby Slowik__.

The good news is that four starters return for Miami. LT __Patrick Paul__ performed better than expected in both phases, RT __Austin Jackson__ was fine returning from injury, and C __Aaron Brewer__ was one of the best centers in football. That said, RG __Jonah Savaiinaea__ was a huge weak link, particularly in protection. He moves over to the right side after being arguably the worst LG in the NFL in 2025.

His replacement at LG is first-round pick __Kadyn Proctor__. I was a big fan of the Alabama product in the lead-up to the draft. He’s a freakishly athletic dude for his size, has the strength to grind down defenders, and can kick outside if needed. He certainly needs to refine some aspects of his game, but Miami got a steal with Proctor at No. 12.

I need to see it before I believe that Miami’s offensive line will pick up Slowik’s system, but this group overachieved last year, has a lot of continuity, and adds a solid rookie to the mix.

#### 23\. __Washington Commanders__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 11

##### Projected Starting Lineup

LT __Laremy Tunsil / Brandon Coleman__

LG __Chris Paul / Timothy McKay__

C __Nick Allegretti__

RG __Sam Cosmi / Andrew Wylie__

RT __Josh Conerly Jr.__

Talk about a flop. I had the Commanders' OL pushing the top 10 heading into last year, after an impressive 2024 campaign. But Jayden Daniels’ injury magnified __an entire__ team regression, and the unit finished with a large split between run and pass performance. There are multiple moving parts up front, but the silver lining is that everyone was on the team last year.

__Laremy Tunsil__ continues to be a force on the edge and must be the anchor of this unit in 2026. __Josh Conerly__ was serviceable as a rookie, but there’s a lot of work to be done in both phases. The interior is where the movement is, as __Nick Allegretti__ replaces __Tyler Biadasz__ at center, and __Sam Cosmi__ returns after an injury-riddled 2025. Cosmi was good in the games he played, but will he return to form?

__Chris Paul__ is also back at LG, but he had arguably the biggest split between pass pro and run blocking. It’s frankly surprising the Commanders averaged the fifth-best YPC (4.73) despite having one of the worst run-blocking left guards.

It’s not a secret that 2026 is important for many within the Commanders’ organization. I think this unit and the offense as a whole bounce back, but it will be a battle for Washington to make the playoffs.

Was 2025 a blip or the new way of things for Kansas City? The Chiefs were a bottom-half rushing team and one of the worst in protection last year, yet they return four full-time starters.

C __Creed Humphrey__ and RG __Trey Smith__ anchor the unit, with Humphrey being the best center in the league last year, and LG __Kingsley Suamataia__ was serviceable in his first year as a starter. LT __Josh Simmons__ had an interesting run-pass split as a rookie, performing much better-than-expected in protection. Can he build on it?

The major change is at RT, as the __Jawaan Taylor__ experiment officially failed. __Jaylon Moore__ saw time at both tackle spots last year, and was flat-out bad in protection. __Esa Pole__ and rookie free agent __Kahlil Benson__ are the reserve tackles, so Moore should get a bit of a leash this year.

#### 25\. __Pittsburgh Steelers__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 29

LG __Mason McCormick / Gennings Dunker \*__

C __Zach Frazier__

RT __Dylan Cook / Max Iheanachor \*__

Much like with Houston, I wasn’t a huge fan of Pittsburgh’s offensive line heading into last season. There was a lot of youth to get excited about, but the overall unit somewhat flopped in __Aaron Rodgers__’ first year as a Steeler. __Mike McCarthy__ (huh???) takes over as head coach, so there’s hope that he and Rodgers can get the spark back for one more season.

__Zach Frazier__ and __Mason McCormick__ anchor the unit as one of the best center-guard pairs in the league. These two came to Pittsburgh together in the 2024 draft and have been above-average each of the last two seasons. McCormick is moving to the left side this year. __Troy Fautanu__ also came to the Steelers in 2024 and was fine on the right side last season. He’s bumped __Broderick Jones__ out at LT, so the Steelers believe he can get the job done, but I expected a bigger step forward last year.

The questions are with RG __Spencer Anderson__ and RT __Dylan Cook__. Each saw some playing time in 2025, but neither was in a starting role. Expect both to be in preseason battles with free agent __Brock Hoffman__ and 2026 draft pick __Gennings Dunker__. Dunker will start his career at guard, but he played tackle at Iowa and has the right mentality for a Steelers lineman. The wild card is first-round pick __Max Iheanachor__. I really liked how much he improved over the course of last season at Arizona State, but there’s still a lot of rawness to his game. The plan could be to redshirt Iheanachor in 2026, but I wouldn’t be surprised if he saw some time this year.

Pittsburgh has a lot to work with up front. Everyone is young and talented, but will the group struggle to handle the Rodgers-McCarthy dynamic? I expect a better overall season from this unit, but there will likely be hiccups.

Cincinnati’s offensive line had a forgettable 2025. The unit was awful in pass protection and below average in run blocking. The Bengals were snake-bit by their defense, but the offensive line was a close second as the team’s worst unit. It’s shocking to me that there weren’t more changes up front this offseason. How hot is __Zac Taylor__’s seat?

The silver lining is that there’s plenty of experience and continuity for this group. __Orlando Brown__, __Ted Karras__, and __Dalton Risner__ each have at least seven years of experience, and Risner was more than capable as a late-training-camp addition. That said, Risner was the best of the three last year, as Brown and Karras underperformed.

The youth elements of Cincinnati’s OL are LG __Dylan Fairchild__ and RT __Amarius Mims__. I’m a fan of Mims and how athletic he is for his size, but both need to take another step forward in 2026, particularly in the run game. I also like what Cincinnati did in the draft, bringing in __Connor Lew__ and __Brian Parker II__. Lew was my favorite center, and Parker should be a quality depth piece early in his career. I’d expect Parker to see time first, but both could get on the field this season.

If the Bengals get average offensive line play, __Joe Burrow__ will take care of the rest, but this unit needs to be significantly better in 2026.

A lot has changed in Tennessee since I wrote this article last year. __Brian Callahan__ is out, and __Robert Saleh__ is a head coach again. Along with Saleh comes __Brian Daboll__, the new offensive coordinator, and a new offensive mentality for the Titans. By the numbers, Tennessee’s OL wasn’t terrible in 2025, but how much will Daboll’s scheme improve the new-look unit in 2026?

The returners are LT __Dan Moore__, LG __Pete Skoronski__, and RT __J.C. Latham__. Skoronski was clearly the best of the group in both phases, with Latham adding quality to the run game and Moore being capable, albeit not outstanding. These three will have to be solid for __Cam Ward__ as they, along with the two new starters, learn Daboll’s system.

The new guys are C __Austin Schlottmann__ and RG __Cordell Volson,__ who come over from the Giants and Bengals, respectively. Schlottmann put together a quality season on limited reps in both phases for New York, but Volson is coming off a preseason shoulder injury and didn’t play at all in 2025.

There are a lot of moving parts for Ward to get used to, and he’ll have to rely on his offensive line picking things up quickly. I think this unit ends up in the middle of the pack, but Daboll should make the Titans more exciting to watch on offense.

I don’t think things will go well overall, but there are some positives up front.

Starting with the 2025 bright spots, RT __Armand Membou__ stepped in and performed very well as a rookie. Steady free agent __Dylan Parham__ comes over from Las Vegas at LG.

As for the question marks, LT __Olu Fashanu__ hasn’t lived up to his first-round pedigree yet. There’s still time for the young tackle, but he really struggled in the run game last year. C __Josh Myers__ returns and should probably be up for replacement after below-average performances in both phases in 2025.

Seemingly like always, the Jets have a lot of moving pieces up front and a new quarterback under center. This offense needs to find an identity and stick to it. New York could run the ball last year (8th in YPC, 4.60), but was one of the worst in protection. That was partially quarterback-driven, but something needs to be figured out up front quickly enough to save the head coach’s job.

Meanwhile, C __John Michael Schmitz__ and LG __Jon Runyan__ were below-average in both phases. Stroud__’s year two regression, and things seemed to be heading down a similar path last season. The Texans struggled to run the ball all year (3.90 YPC), but this group surprised me by finishing middle-of-the-road in protection. Will year two of __Nick Caley__’s offense be different?

The two returning starters are LT __Aireontae Ersery__ and RG __Ed Ingram__. Ersery is on the way up after gaining a ton of experience as a rookie, and Ingram wound up starting 14 games. However, the Texans are once again hoping that a major shakeup will create lasting success with three new starters in 2026.

Rookie C __Keylan Rutledge__ is slated to start, but don’t be surprised if veteran __Jake Andrews__ sees time. __Braden Smith__ (Colts), __Wyatt Teller__ (Browns), and __Evan Brown__ (Cardinals) all come over in free agency and will be in position battles at RT (Smith and __Trent Brown__) and RG, respectively. Stroud is once again in a tough situation, as yet again he’ll have to get comfortable with a shaken-up offensive line. Houston picked up his fifth-year option, but I think it’s “put up or shut up” for Stroud this season, despite the new-look OL. 2026 feels like another season of the Texans relying on the defense.

#### 31\. __Las Vegas Raiders__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 22

LT __Kolton Miller__

LG __Spencer Burford $__

RG __Jackson Powers-Johnson / Caleb Rodgers__

RT __D.J. Glaze__

Las Vegas’ offensive line was arguably the biggest disappointment in the league last season. I didn’t think they’d be excellent, but __Ashton Jeanty__ was a shell of himself as a rookie, and the unit produced the worst YPC in the NFL (3.57). Moves had to be made up front, and the Raiders did that by adding __Tyler Linderbaum__ and (to a lesser extent) __Spencer Burford__. How well will __Klint Kubiak__’s Super Bowl-winning offense translate to Las Vegas?

LT __Kolton Miller__ is slated to return after missing most of last year with an ankle injury. He was on track for an excellent season in both phases in year eight. __Jackson Powers-Johnson__ is also returning from a season-ending ankle injury, but wasn’t doing as well as Miller. All-name team __D.J. Glaze__ also returns at RT after a subpar 2025.

There was clearly a lot of room to improve for this unit, and giving Linderbaum $81 million over three years should prove that. He had a fairly large run-pass split last season, but this will be a quality move for the Raiders. That said, the Burford signing feels like Vegas was stuck wanting a vet but didn't have the money, as the former 49er ranked near the bottom in protection last season.

Linderbaum signals that Vegas is ready to invest in its new quarterback. __Fernando Mendoza__ will have enough to deal with as a rookie once he eventually plays, and giving him a quality center is a step in the right direction. In the interim, __Kirk Cousins__ can take a beating while the line tries to pull itself together.

I think this unit takes a step forward, but not enough to make the playoffs this year.

#### 32\. __Cleveland Browns__ – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 17

LG __Zion Johnson $__

C __Elgton Jenkins $ / Parker Brailsford \*__

RG __Teven Jenkins__

RT __Tytus Howard $ / Austin Barber \*__

Talk about a new look. Cleveland returns no preseason projected starters from last season, after investing money and picks in its offensive line. Three stalwarts (__Joel Bitonio__, __Jack Conklin__, and __Ethan Pocic__) are gone, and new head coach __Todd Monken__ is tasked with rebuilding the offense from the ground up.

RG __Teven Jenkins__ returns for another year after starting four of the final five games in 2025. He was surprisingly good in the run game, and will have to be again for Monken. Big __Dawand Jones__ also returns but has been relegated to a backup role heading into the season.

Starting with the new vets, Cleveland traded for __Tytus Howard__ and signed __Zion Johnson__ and __Elgton Jenkins__ in free agency. None of the three are particularly good run blockers, so we’ll have to wait and see how Monken adjusts his attack.

The Browns also added three draft picks: __Spencer Fano__, __Austin Barber__, and __Parker Brailsford.__ Fano was my No. 1 lineman this year and will begin his career at LT. Barber and Brailsford will begin as depth pieces, but with so many new faces there’s a halfway decent chance they get on the field in some capacity. 2026 is figure it out as you go for the Browns’ OL.
